name: ANSI/IEEE thermometer symbol
summary: IEEE-library thermometer instrument form for a local or panel temperature reading taken from a sensor input.
description: The thermometer form is an indicating instrument circle whose input is a temperature sensor rather than a power circuit. On control schematics it sits at the end of a thermocouple, RTD or transmitter loop, so the important connections are the sensor wiring and any compensation or lead-resistance arrangement.

The symbol identifies indication only. Alarm and trip set points belong to separate switch or relay contacts, and the measuring range, sensor type and accuracy class must be read from the instrument schedule because the circle carries none of that information.
readingNotes: Follow the input back to the sensor and note its type (thermocouple, RTD or transmitter).
Look for separate contacts if the instrument also gives alarms.
drawingChecklist: Name the sensor and its location
Reference any alarm or trip contacts
distinction: A thermometer indicates temperature; a temperature switch changes contact state at a set point and may have no display at all.
